name: The Bony Fish Fossils of the Western Limfjord – Evolution and Climate Adaptation in the Earliest Eocene
description: On the shores of the Limfjord in northern Jutland, the coastal cliffs of Hanklit and Knudeklint hold some of the best-preserved fossil fishes anywhere. Their layers of diatom-rich clay and volcanic ash captured more than 80 fish species, plus sea turtles, birds, insects and plants, from the early Eocene. Together they show how life recovered after the dinosaurs' extinction and coped with a sudden global warming.
